scores.claim_text: Net sales increased 7% to $60.4B in fiscal 2026; consolidated comp sales +5%.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts brand mention asymmetric test: 'T.J. Maxx' phrase, no CIK restriction; 'TJX' bare query.
scores.M_value: T.J. Maxx: 180 hits across 10-K/10-Q corpus pre-cutoff; TJX: 969 hits across 10-K/10-Q corpus pre-cutoff. Strong external presence consistent with a $60B-revenue retailer.
scores.interpretation: Healthy retailer profile. No M-side contradiction; brand has broad SEC corpus footprint consistent with claimed scale. Internal claim about +5% comps is non-falsifiable via external sources but consistent with multi-year off-price tailwinds. No distress signal.

scores.claim_text: Operates over 5,200 stores at end of fiscal 2026; store count and selling sqft both up ~3% YoY.
scores.M_check: Brand asymmetric mention test on banner names 'TK Maxx' (international banner only) and 'HomeGoods' (U.S. banner).
scores.M_value: TK Maxx: 14 hits (concentrated in TJX's own filings — narrow international banner exposure). HomeGoods: 978 hits — top filers include Brixmor (BRX), Kimco Realty (KIM) and other shopping-center REITs as tenant disclosures.
scores.interpretation: Landlord 10-Ks corroborate HomeGoods as a meaningful retail tenant. State-by-state store count table in Item 2 of the 10-K sums to 3,790 U.S. stores + 589 Canada + 747 Europe + 88 Australia + 145 Sierra (in Marmaxx) = 5,214 total, internally consistent with 'over 5,200' headline. No mass-closure 8-K signal in the filings index for fiscal 2026. Calibration Heuristic 11 (store-count trajectory): PASS.

scores.claim_text: TJX is a major tenant in U.S. retail real estate; virtually all 3,790 U.S. stores leased, with typical 10-year initial terms.
scores.M_check: Counterparty test: do mall REIT landlords disclose TJX as a tenant? Tried 'TJX' bare and banner names ('Marshalls', 'T.J. Maxx', 'HomeGoods') against SPG (CIK 0001063761) and MAC (CIK 0000912242). Calibration Heuristic 6 (name-variant fragility) applied.
scores.M_value: SPG: 0 hits for 'TJX' but 17 hits each for 'Marshalls', 'T.J. Maxx', 'HomeGoods' (banner-level disclosure). MAC: 0 hits across all four terms. Brixmor (BRX) and Kimco (KIM) surfaced in C2 HomeGoods query.
scores.interpretation: Simon Property Group strongly corroborates TJX as a multi-banner tenant. Macerich absence is consistent with TJX's predominant footprint in power centers / community centers / strip centers (Brixmor, Kimco) rather than Class A enclosed malls (Macerich's specialty). Counterparty disclosure threshold (Heuristic 7) MET. Banner names rather than 'TJX' parent ticker is the M-side convention. No contradiction.

scores.claim_text: TJX's opportunistic buying model sources from a broad global vendor base; sells branded merchandise at 20-60% off full-price retailers.
scores.M_check: Apparel-supplier counterparty test: do HBI, LEVI, VFC, TPR 10-Ks name TJX or its banners? Tried multiple banner variants + 'off-price' generic.
scores.M_value: HBI 'T.J. Maxx': 2 hits. LEVI 'off-price': 3 hits. VFC 'off-price': 2 hits. TPR 'TJX': 3 hits. All other combinations: 0.
scores.interpretation: Low but non-zero supplier mentions are CONSISTENT with TJX's stated opportunistic-buying model. Off-price retailers are not contractual top-customer relationships — they're channels suppliers use for excess/closeout. The 'off-price' generic mentions in LEVI/VFC 10-Ks corroborate the existence of the channel even when TJX isn't named directly. Calibration Heuristic 7 (counterparty disclosure threshold) is below the bar for HARD CONTRADICTION because TJX does not claim to be a TOP customer of any single supplier (it claims breadth/opportunism). Severity PASS but with note: this M-source has limited discriminative power for off-price retailers.

scores.claim_text: Strong liquidity ($6.2B cash, $1.5B revolver, no short-term borrowings); $4.3B returned to shareholders in FY26; new $3B repurchase authorization. Recognized $419M gain from credit-card interchange-fee litigation settlement.
scores.M_check: Layer 3 Rule 10 direct distress-marker test: (a) search TJX's own filings for 'going concern'; (b) confirm interchange-litigation context via Visa 10-K; (c) check AmEx for TJX disclosure.
scores.M_value: TJX 'going concern': 8 hits — all from 2020 (COVID-era revolver/credit-agreement exhibits, boilerplate event-of-default covenant language; NOT auditor going-concern qualifiers). Visa 'interchange': 9 hits in Visa 10-Ks pre-cutoff (corroborates the merchant-interchange litigation context that produced TJX's $419M settlement gain). AXP 'TJX': 0 hits (consistent — AmEx 10-K does not disclose individual large merchants by name).
scores.interpretation: No going-concern qualifier, no form-15-12G, no 25-NSE, no covenant-waiver 8-K in the filings index. The 2020 hits are routine credit-agreement boilerplate, not financial distress. Visa interchange context independently corroborates the $419M settlement gain TJX booked. Severity PASS — this is a textbook healthy-retailer balance sheet. Calibration Heuristic 10 (delisting/going-concern): CLEAR. Functions as the cohort control.

scores.claim_text: Planned international expansion: Spain (March 2026 TK Maxx launch); Mexico JV with Grupo Axo; minority equity investment in BFL (Middle East). Capex $2.2-2.3B guided for FY27.
scores.M_check: Planned-vs-operational test (Calibration Heuristic 3). (a) External corroboration of Grupo Axo JV partner; (b) Internal consistency of Spain claim across multi-period TJX filings.
scores.M_value: Grupo Axo: 82 hits across SEC corpus pre-cutoff, including Nike 8-K (Feb 2020) and Ulta Beauty 8-K (Aug 2025) — Grupo Axo is a well-known LatAm brand operator that has been a JV/licensing partner for multiple U.S. retailers, corroborating it as a real counterparty. TJX 'Spain': 8 hits across TJX's own filings — includes FY25 10-K (April 2025), Q3-FY25 earnings 8-K (Nov 2024), and FY26 10-K (March 2026). The Spain plan has been disclosed across multiple periods, not a one-off marketing claim.
scores.interpretation: Spain expansion has stage-ladder evidence: announced in FY25 Q3 (Nov 2024) -> reiterated in FY25 10-K (April 2025) -> reiterated as 'starting in March 2026' in FY26 10-K (March 2026). This is the operational-end of Heuristic 3 — execution-window claim, not just promise. Grupo Axo partner externally validated. PASS.
